To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
steroid-BSAs injected intravenously enter the hormone-target cells and are accumulated in the nuclei of those cells with their antigenicity kept intact.

steroid-BSA conjugated with steroid hormones can enter the hormone target cell nuclei with the antigenicity intact, and that steroid-BSAs are taken up by the steroid hormone receptor cells and the steroid hormone target cells at the cell membrane, and then transported into the nucleus.

steroid-BSA conjugated with steroid hormones, such as testosterone, hydrocorti- sone and corticosterone, can enter the hormone target cell nuclei with its immunoreactivity kept intact, and the fate of steroid hormone-BSAs is determined at the level of the cell membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunohistochemical localization of bovines serum albumin ( BSA ) in the liver and tests of rats injected with steroid hormone-BSAs.
the fate of steroid hormones in the hormone-target cells.
the mechanism of hormone action at the cellular level, and the results obtained are useful for the development of new hormone delivery systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
steroid-BSAs are taken up by hormone-target cells and transported to the nucleus, and then are released from the nucleus.
steroid-BSAs can enter steroid hormone target cell nuclei with the antigenicity of BSA kept intact.
BSA conjugates of steroid hormones enter the hormone-target cells, but not the other cells of the liver and testicles, and the fate of BSA is decided at the level of the cell membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

steroid-BSAs can be taken into the nuclei of steroid hormone-target cells, and that the steroid hormone-steroid-BSA complex is released from the steroid-BSAs into the nucleus, and that the hormone-target cell is regulated by this complex.

the steroid-BSAs are taken up by the hormone-target cells through a specific receptor, and are then degraded in the lysosomes, and that the BSA moiety of the steroid-BSA is transferred to the nucleus by an as yet unknown process.
the steroid hormones are delivered to the target cell nuclei in their native form, and then they act as hormones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the steroid-BSAs injected into the rat vascular system enter the steroid hormone-target cell nuclei and remain there with their immunoreactivity intact.
the steroid hormone- BSA conjugate can enter the hormone target cell nuclei and that the fate (whether or not to enter the nucleus) of steroid-BSA is decided at the membrane level.
the nature of BSB in steroid-BSAs remains intact in the steroid-target cell nuclei.
